blocking.issue: W8-host-2 (never cut): the paged ETag read misses an item added after an exactly full last page, and says nothing changed. In pagedConditional, a page answered 304 is served from the copy with the copy's Link header. When the last page held exactly pageSize items and one more is added at the end (comments are oldest first), page 1's body does not change, so its ETag does not either. The stand-in answers 304, the adapter reuses the old Link (no next page), never asks for page 2, and listIssueComments returns notModified: true with the old list. The port promises the opposite: 'notModified says whether anything changed since'. capabilities.md says 'A list's ETag joins its pages' ETags, so it changes when any page changes', which does not hold for an appended page. The contract's paging case uses 105 comments and never hits this boundary.
blocking.evidence:
Stand-in probe (`/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/9d17d664-b8c3-5e0d-8f13-1f917f72dcc2/scratchpad/probe2/page-boundary.mts`, run with pnpm exec tsx):
- pageSize 3: 'after one more comment, same client: 3 comments, notModified = true'; 'a fresh client reads: 4 comments'; requests [per_page=3 200, per_page=3 304, then the fresh client's per_page=3 200 and page=2 200].
- pageSize 100 (production default): 'after one more comment, same client: 100 comments, notModified = true'; 'a fresh client reads: 101 comments'.
On the bench (`/tmp/frbench/review-w8-issue-host/steps/adapter-probe.json`), the 101st comment was Bob's 'I now work on the menu too'. Ada's GitHubHost, reading through her proxy with the earlier etag, gave {count: 100, notModified: true}; a fresh client gave 101.
Failure for D9: once a status issue holds a multiple of 100 comments, a new writer's announcement stays invisible to the other Forerunner's poller. Its reader (w8-status-read) skips work on notModified. This lasts until something on page 1 changes, so Bob's work can be done twice. The same holds for listIssues with direction asc, and for any list w8-github-feed moves onto pagedConditional, as the report suggests.
blocking.expected: A conditional paged read never says not modified while an item exists past its copied last page. For example: when a page is served from the copy, holds a full page (length === pageSize) and the copy has no next link, also read page N+1 (or read the last full page without If-None-Match). Add a contract case on the stand-in over HTTP: a GitHubHost with a small pageSize (2 or 3); exactly pageSize comments, read, add one, read with the etag; expect notModified false and every comment. It should fail before the fix. Correct the capabilities.md sentence.

claims_checked.claim: W8-host-1: the port has getIssue, listIssues (paged, creator/labels/sort/direction), listIssueComments with authors and an ETag, getIssueComment (null when deleted), updateIssueComment (keeps the mark, no delete), pinIssue (pinned/limit/forbidden), getRepoPermission and RepoInfo.hasIssues; IssueInfo and IssueCommentInfo carry the fields listed, with no editor field.
claims_checked.note: Read in types.ts, github.ts and memory.ts. The contract passes on both stand-ins and fails before the fix. The bench probe confirms pinned → limit at three and the field set.

claims_checked.claim: W8-host-2: ETag reads with If-None-Match; a 304 answered from an in-memory LRU (500) keyed by the token hash and URL; paged lists past 100; nothing on disk; a next page on another origin is refused before the token goes there.
claims_checked.note: The ETag, 304, per-token key, other-origin refusal and paging past 100 all hold (tests, and the bench log shows ifNoneMatch). But the paged conditional read gives a false notModified at an exactly full last page (blocking 1), so 'notModified says whether anything changed' does not hold in general.

claims_checked.claim: W8-host-3: the stand-in gives ETags and 304 (with a rate-limit refund), has_issues and 410 on issue routes (pull request comments stay on), sort/direction, associations from owner/org/collaborators, a Bot type for [bot] logins, the permission route (404 without push access), and POST /graphql with StatusPinnedIssues/StatusPinIssue and at most three pins.
claims_checked.note: Read routes-graphql.ts, routes-collaborators.ts, routes-issues.ts, store.ts and fake-git-host.ts. githost.test.ts passes (8 cases fail without the fix). The raw probe on my bench reproduces each answer.

claims_checked.claim: W8-host-4: MemoryGitHost implements the same calls with the seams setOrg, setCollaboratorRole, setIssuesEnabled, pinnedIssues and removeIssueComment; association is worked out at each read; an edit moves updatedAt; writes are recorded.
claims_checked.note: The memory contract describe passes (10 cases fail before). A repository with no roles declared answers 'write' for every login, as documented.

claims_checked.claim: W8-host-5: listIssues by creator and label, sorted by updated; newestCommentPerAuthor from one paged read.
claims_checked.note: Contract case passes on both stand-ins; the bench probe confirms newestCommentPerAuthor.

claims_checked.claim: W8-host-6: a new issues_disabled code for 'Issues are disabled' 410; a deleted issue's 410 is not_found; a 404 on createIssue in a repository the token sees is marked no_permission; issueRefusalOf maps every reason; details.status is kept; older codes are unchanged.
claims_checked.note: Stub cases pass, and the stand-in's 410 and 403 cases pass. The stand-in itself never produces the 404-as-no-permission reason; this is in not_done with a reason, and W8-host-6 is not a never-cut item. The 404 probe applies to createIssue only.

claims_checked.claim: The status-issue injection case belongs to w8-status-read, not this area.
claims_checked.note: wave8-plan.json puts the record-channel status-issue case in w8-status-read (W8-read-8) and w8-status-write. This area hands no issue text to a model; its contract has a case where a comment giving orders comes back verbatim.

non_blocking: pinIssue calls getIssue outside its try block, so a 403 or 401 on that read throws tool_not_allowed or provider_auth instead of answering 'forbidden' (github.ts pinIssue). The re-read after UNPROCESSABLE (three pins taken in a race) is never tested: the adapter checks the pin count first, so the contract never reaches it. A fetch-stub case would cover it.

W8-host-6's 404-as-no_permission probe exists only on createIssue. A 404 on commentOnIssue or updateIssueComment in a repository the token sees reads as 'missing'. On GitHub these are usually 403, so the harm is small; the w8-status-write caller should know about it.

conditionalGet reads the token for the cache key and request() reads it again. If the vault token changes between the two reads, the answer is stored under the old token's key. The window is tiny and the next read with the new token is a full 200 anyway.

Stand-in fidelity: HostStore.affiliations(login, 'write') now leaves out orgs whose base permission is read, and canCreateRepo uses those affiliations, so a read-base member can no longer create repositories in the org. On GitHub that is a separate member privilege. No current test depends on it.

The fixer's new_problems hold. The repository-wide GET /repos/:o/:r/issues/comments is shadowed by /issues/:number, so it is always 404 (this predates the area), and the new issuesOn(repo) on it can never be reached. repoJson's permissions.admin is still loose for collaborators; w8-shared-repo should read the role through roleOf.

I did not re-run Playwright (no UI code changed in this area; the fixer reports 40 passed). I walked one bench (Ada) because of the one-bench rule; the two-person screens are the fixer's (15/30 both before and after, no failure outside the known gaps).

Live check for the session lead (in addition to the fixer's steps): on the sandbox issue, post exactly 100 comments, call listIssueComments(repo, n), add a 101st, then call listIssueComments(repo, n, {etag}). Record whether GitHub answers page 1 with a 304 (it would if its ETag covers only the body). That shows how real GitHub behaves at the boundary in blocking 1.
